text.p: - The Slovenian government has refused to raise petrol prices.
- A group of Slovenian officials, charged with negotiating the succession of former Yugoslavia's assets, met Sir Arthur Watts in Brussels on Thursday.
- The board of national radio and television has nominated Janez Cadez as its general manager.

- The alliance of three rightist "Spring" parties said they have already gained the one parliamentary seat needed for an absolute majority. The group, comprising the conservative People's Party, centre-right Social Democrats and Christian Democrats, received 45 out of 90 seats in Slovenia's second general election on November 10.
- The European Bank of Reconstruction and Development said Slovenia is one of the most developed among transition countries.

- Leader of leftist United List of social Democrats, which received nine seats in a 90 seat parliament on last general election said on Thursday, his party will support current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek's efforts to remain on his post.
- Debts of car parts producer Cimos reached about 30 billion tolars ($218.9 million), the company's management said on Thursday.
- Pharmaceutical producer Krka on Thursday gave awards to 40 student researchers for their chemical and pharmaceutical research.

- The Liberal Democrats spent 12.4 million tolars ($90,510) and the Christian Democrats 10.5 million tolars on their election campaigns. The two parties were the leading spenders in the run-up to the country's second general election.
